assessment.rationale: A 1:42 half predicts roughly a 3:32-3:36 marathon, and a 3:00 would require about a 1:26 half-level fitness, which is unattainable in 12 weeks from 20 miles/week with an 8-mile long run on 4 days/week. Building to ~40 miles/week with a 18-20 mile long run is realistic, so target about 3:35 and revisit a sub-3:00 goal after a full training cycle.

A 1:42 half predicts roughly a 3:32-3:35 marathon, and a 3:00 would require about 25 minutes of improvement, which is not achievable in 12 weeks from 20 miles/week with an 8-mile long run on 4 days/week. Building safely to a ~40 mpw peak with a 18-20 mile long run supports a 3:35 target, with 3:30 as a stretch if training goes well.

A 1:48:00 half predicts roughly 3:46-3:50 for a marathon, and 3:30:00 (8:00/mile pace) would need a much stronger base than 25 miles/week with a 12-mile long run can build in 10 weeks. A 3:45:00 target (about 8:35/mile) is achievable with a peak near 40 miles/week and a 20-mile long run, and a late-race surge could still be reserved if the day goes well.

A 1:48 half predicts roughly a 3:45 marathon at best, and with only 25 mpw, a 12-mile long run and 10 weeks to build, 3:30 (8:00/mi) is too aggressive. Build to about 40 mpw with 18-20 mile long runs, and a 3:45-3:50 goal is realistic.

A 1:30:00 half predicts roughly 3:07-3:12 for the marathon, and 18 weeks at 6 days/week is enough to build from 35 to about 52 miles with 18-20 mile long runs. The goal is realistic but not guaranteed given the modest mileage base, so reassess with a tune-up half around week 10 and fall back to about 3:13 if it comes in slower than 1:29.

A 1:30 half predicts roughly 3:08-3:12 for the marathon, and 18 weeks at 6 days/week is enough to build from 35 to about 50-55 miles with 20-mile long runs. The goal is achievable but aggressive for the current base, so treat 3:12-3:13 as the fallback if the 16-20 mile long runs at marathon pace feel strained.

A 2:12 half predicts roughly 4:35 to 4:40 for a well-trained runner, so 4:30 (10:18/mi) is already optimistic. With only 15 mpw and a 6-mile long run, a 16-week, 4-day build that peaks near 36 mpw and a 20-mile long run likely won't support that pace, so 4:40 is a safer target, with 4:30 as a stretch if training goes perfectly.

A 2:12 half predicts about 4:35 for a well-trained marathoner, but a 15 mpw base and 6-mile long run leave 16 weeks to build to roughly 35 mpw and an 18-20 mile long run on 4 days a week, which makes 4:30 (10:18/mi) a stretch. A 4:45 goal is safer, and you can push toward 4:30-4:35 only if long runs and race-pace workouts go well.

A 1:23:30 half predicts roughly 2:54-2:56 for the marathon, so 2:55:00 is right at the edge of current fitness. With 20 weeks, a build from 45 to about 60 mpw, long runs up to 20-22 miles and plenty of marathon-pace work, it is achievable. I'd plan around 2:56 and go for 2:55 only if the build goes well and race-day conditions are good.

A 1:23:30 half predicts roughly 2:54-2:56 for the marathon (about 6:41/mi for 2:55), and 20 weeks at 6 days/week is enough to build from 45 to about 60 mpw with 18-20 mile long runs and marathon-pace work. The goal is realistic but has little margin, so run the first half conservatively and treat 2:57 as the fallback if training stalls or the half-marathon fitness doesn't hold up in the long runs.

A 1:50 half predicts about 3:49 at best, but with only 30 miles/week, a 14-mile long run and 8 weeks to build, the endurance base is likely to fall short, so 3:45 (8:35/mi) is a high-risk target. A 3:55 goal is more realistic: build to about 40 miles/week with a peak long run of 20 miles, and run the first half conservatively, with 3:45 as a stretch only if the race goes very well.

A 1:50 half predicts about 3:49 for a marathon with full marathon training, and 30 mpw with a 14-mile long run and only 8 weeks to build leaves little room to reach that, so 3:45 (8:35/mi) is a stretch. Build to about 40 mpw with long runs up to 20 miles, and aim for around 3:52, going out at 8:50-8:55/mi and speeding up in the last 10K only if you feel good.
